scope: Object-track-grounded robot appearance, topology, and projected-contact audit of two 27.5-second candidates
summary: The audit rejects v6 late color/identity drift and selects the legacy robot layer, but the selected layer narrowly misses the hand-replacement gate before repair.
evidence: v6 violates its late high-chroma limit on 81.67% of frames and its canonical-palette limit on 100% of frames.
v6 projected-contact recall after 20 seconds is 11/12, or 91.67%.
The selected stable layer has zero late high-chroma and palette violations and 12/12 projected contacts, but hand-replacement violations are 11.67% against a 10% limit.
Color-shift, arm-erasure, and hand-detachment attacks are detected for both candidates over 101 sampled/adversarial frames.
lessons: A single temporal score hides distinct appearance, topology, and interaction failures.
Late thresholds must be fit on an accepted anchor interval rather than on the failing tail itself.
limitations: Replacement coverage is an image-space topology proxy and cannot identify all finger morphs.
Projected contact is not depth, force, or executable-robot contact.
next_actions: Repair only the failed hand support while protecting source flowers, then rerun the unchanged blind gates.
